What winners share

Every day, every graded over at Hard Rock, Novig and Kalshi (tracked tags, slate picks, every parlay leg) and every cross-game parlay, sorted by what they had in common before the game. Updated 2026-11-14 21:01 UTC · results through Sat Nov 14.

How to read this

A trait found in most winners is usually just a short price: favorites win most of the time and fill every list of winners. So each trait is judged against its price: won vs priced (wins vs what the odds implied) and the return at $1 a bet, in both halves of the last 30 days. About 220 traits are checked every day, so a few will look good by luck. That is why the forward check matters most: the day a trait first clears the bar it is written down, and from then on it is graded only on bets settled after that day. A trait that keeps beating its price there is a real lead for leg selection; it still needs the owner’s OK before any card uses it.

Display only: no card, tag or bet rule reads this page. Data: markets/traits.json.

Everything the site recommends, graded at the price it showed, 1 unit per bet. Prediction-market picks follow the site's rules on the last pregame quote (Kalshi includes its fee); Value tags use the tagged book's price when the tag first appeared, and Beat close compares it with that book's last price before the game; for prediction-market picks Beat close is Pinnacle's fair (no-vig) closing chance minus the price paid, fee included, when Pinnacle priced the same bet (positive = better than the sharpest closing line, the quickest sign of a real edge); parlays are every card on the Plays / Parlays tabs, frozen before their first game. Verdicts: Proven = the 95% range of the return is above zero (30+ bets; the range counts bets on the same day as moving together) and the rule still stands after allowing for how many rules are being tested (Benjamini-Hochberg, 10% false-discovery rate); Not bettable = graded at a price no book pays (our own fair, or same-game legs multiplied); totals count each bet once; Losing = below zero; Promising = beats the closing line by a clear margin; Too early = fewer than 30 bets. Skill vs mkt = 1 − Brier score of our chance ÷ Brier score of the market’s chance on the same bets (the market’s fair with the vig out for tags, Kalshi’s price paid without the fee for prediction-market picks): above 0 means our chance forecast these bets better than the price did, with its 95% range.
